title: IDF Airstrike Kills 5 at Hamas Police Post Adjacent to Displaced Persons Tent Camp, Khan Younis
detail: An Israeli airstrike struck a Hamas-run police post adjacent to a large tent camp of displaced families in Khan Younis on June 7, 2026, killing at least 5 Palestinians and wounding 16 more. The strike occurred as Egyptian-mediated ceasefire talks were under way in Cairo. The strike on a police post in close proximity to a major displacement camp drew condemnation from humanitarian organizations, who noted the recurring IDF pattern of targeting Hamas police infrastructure in areas densely populated with displaced civilians. The UN OHCHR has documented at least 12 attacks on police posts since January 2026, killing 53+ civilians including 35 police personnel. The latest strike brings the cumulative Palestinian death toll under the October 2025 ceasefire to approximately 965+ since October 11, 2025.

media.caption: Israeli airstrike kills 5 at police post near displaced persons camp in Khan Younis — June 7, 2026

title: Second IDF Airstrike Kills 4 in Vehicle Strike, Central Gaza City
detail: A second Israeli airstrike struck a vehicle in central Gaza City on June 7, 2026, killing 4 Palestinians and wounding 4 more. Combined with the Khan Younis police post strike earlier in the day, at least 9 Palestinians were killed in Israeli strikes on June 7 — the same day Egypt was hosting a new round of ceasefire implementation talks. The vehicle strike and police post attack occurred as Egyptian, Qatari, and Turkish mediators continued shuttle diplomacy in Cairo. The continued IDF operations — combining targeted killing of Hamas personnel with strikes in densely populated areas — are the central point of contention in the ongoing ceasefire talks.

media.caption: IDF vehicle strike kills 4 in central Gaza City as Egypt hosts ceasefire talks — June 7, 2026

title: Hamas Publishes Conditions for Disarmament Talks: 3-Year Phased Timeline, UN Supervision, Israeli Redeployment
detail: Hamas published its formal conditions for any disarmament discussions under Trump's Gaza plan on June 7, 2026. The conditions require: (1) a complete end to Israeli assassinations and targeted killings; (2) Israeli redeployment behind the October 2025 'Yellow Line' ceasefire demarcation; (3) UN-supervised independent Palestinian technocrats to administer Gaza's daily affairs without IDF interference; and (4) a phased 3-year disarmament timeline beginning with surrender of heavy weapons while Hamas retains light arms for self-defense. Israel categorically rejects anything short of full disarmament without preconditions as its position going into Phase 2. The publication of Hamas's formal conditions represents the clearest articulation yet of the parties' incompatible positions, suggesting Phase 2 negotiations remain deeply stalled despite the Cairo talks. Egypt, Qatar, and Turkey are attempting to find a sequencing formula that both parties could accept to begin substantive negotiations.

media.caption: Hamas formally publishes conditions for disarmament talks: 3-year phased timeline, UN supervision — June 7, 2026
